title: Vortex screening and the fate of the BKT transition with long-range couplings
abstract: The stability of the Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless phase against long-range interactions remains an open problem. We address this question in the two-dimensional XY model with couplings decaying as r^{-2-σ}, by developing a real-space renormalization-group treatment near the Gaussian manifold of quasi-long-range ordered (QLRO) states. We retain the full many-body vortex interaction and show that, at leading order in the fugacity, screening by small vortex--antivortex pairs preserves its Gaussian-average representation without an expansion in the long-range coupling. Including spin waves perturbatively then yields a local stability criterion: a stable QLRO interval exists only for σ>7/4. We also investigate a Wilson--Fisher-like fixed point at finite coupling for σ<7/4, for which the retained flow predicts ν^{-1}sim7/4-σ as it merges with the Gaussian line.

title: A Scoping Review and Experimental Study on Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback for Human-Robot Collaboration
abstract: Human-Robot Collaboration (HRC) can facilitate mass customisation in Industry 4.0, with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) representing a promising approach for developing safe AI-based robots. Practical challenges remain regarding safety during AI development, human feedback quality, and bidirectional human-robot adaptation. We conducted a scoping review of RLHF in HRC systems, mapping methods that address these challenges. Following PRISMA guidelines, we screened 199 records and included 20 peer-reviewed publications (2020-2025) spanning multiple HRC domains. To our knowledge, this is the first review focused on the bidirectional, closed-loop design of RLHF. Our review found multiple feedback modalities enabling data collection in various feedback formats. Collected data can be integrated at different stages of AI training, resulting in a multi-step development process. Pilot experiments are commonly used to evaluate HRC systems based on both human and robot metrics. To empirically test a key gap identified in the review, we conducted a between-subjects VR experiment comparing system- and user-initiated feedback on robot proxemic behaviour for safe navigation. Using Bayesian models, we analysed the relation between the collected feedback and safety metrics: psychological safety (post-experiment questionnaire) and physical safety (inverse time-to-collision). Results show that user-initiated feedback captures perceived safety better than system-initiated feedback, indicating that feedback timing directly affects feedback quality. Our review and experiment findings show that RLHF relies on appropriate feedback methods to ensure AI safety in HRC, and future RLHF research should prioritise realistic HRC experiments evaluating the effects of feedback collection methods on relevant human and robot metrics.

title: Shared and structured inputs undermine collective random choice by reasoning AI agents
abstract: Random selection is widely used in resource allocation and auditing, making reliable implementation essential for AI-agent systems. Behavioural tests across six reasoning models uncovered threshold and divisibility rules used in identifier-based choices. For threshold-following GPT-6 Sol and Gemini 3.8 Flash, single-agent measurements prospectively predicted correlated participation under shared identifiers and biased participation under distinct identifiers with common timestamp bits. Changing dates, formats and identifier labels revealed when these predictions held. Explicit instructions to randomize independently reduced but did not eliminate shared-input correlation. To test implications for oversight, we asked four models to select customer requests randomly for human review. GPT-6 Sol approached the target rate while selecting predictably from identifiers; the others rarely selected requests. All four closely followed supplied random draws. These findings expose collective and audit vulnerabilities that selection rates alone miss, making input-dependent bias, correlation and predictability central targets for agent evaluation.

title: GeoPrior-Mamba: Structured Process Priors with Mamba for Fine-Resolution XCO2 Reconstruction
abstract: Reconstructing fine-resolution column-averaged dry-air CO2 (XCO2) fields from sparse satellite observations requires models to infer spatial structure that is only weakly constrained by direct measurements. Existing learning-based methods typically treat environmental covariates as ordinary numerical inputs and must therefore learn heterogeneous source-sink relationships largely from sparse supervision. We introduce GeoPrior-Mamba, a multi-directional Mamba framework augmented with offline language-model-induced structured process priors. Rather than using a language model to predict XCO2, we use it before training to organize relative process knowledge for biospheric uptake, ecosystem respiration, and anthropogenic emissions into deterministic prior tables. These priors are spatially instantiated using geographic, ecological, emission-related, and seasonal information and are adaptively injected into the reconstruction backbone through a lightweight knowledge adapter. Using OCO-2 observations from 2018-2020, GeoPrior-Mamba achieves an RMSE of 0.81 ppm and an R2 of 0.93 on held-out observations, reducing RMSE by 48.2% relative to CAMS background interpolation and by 3.1% relative to Trans-XCO2 under the same evaluation protocol. Ablation experiments show a measurable contribution from the knowledge-prior branch and substantially faster convergence than the knowledge-free Mamba backbone. Independent TCCON evaluation further supports the consistency of the reconstructed fields with ground-based column CO2 measurements. These results suggest that language models can provide a practical mechanism for constructing structured process priors when globally consistent process-response representations are difficult to obtain directly, while remaining outside the numerical prediction loop.

title: RadarML - Lite - Blind Test Release
abstract: This dataset provides the held-out evaluation recordings for the RadarML Lite modulation-recognition hackathon. It contains 171,600 examples, generated from 13,200 source pulses across 660 waveform configurations, covering seven modulation classes: Barker, CW, FMCW, FSK, HYP, NLFM and QUAD.Each source pulse is represented at 13 requested signal-to-noise ratios, from +30 to −30 dB in 5 dB steps. Recordings use a single receiver channel and contain 16,800 complex I/Q samples at 120 MS/s. Signals are stored as interleaved signed 16-bit integers in anonymized NumPy shards.Test pulses are separate from the published RadarML Lite training and validation pulses, with no shared source identities or exact signal duplicates. The same waveform configurations are represented, so evaluation measures recognition of unseen pulses within known configurations.The archive includes a data loader, anonymous sample index, prediction-submission template, checksums and preprocessing diagnostics. Class labels, per-example SNRs and source mappings are withheld for organizer scoring. Participants should use this dataset only after freezing their model and preprocessing.Preprocessing matches the development dataset. SNR values are requested settings rather than guaranteed achieved values; int16 clipping affects approximately 5.38% of I/Q values at −30 dB.Derived from the RadarML dataset by Ritchie, White and Hosford (2025), DOI: 10.5522/04/30752767.v1.

title: Architecture Patterns for Low-Latency Real-Time Voice Agents: Design Patterns, Adoption Gaps, and Operational Lessons from a Production Deployment
abstract: Real-time conversational voice agents, which combine speech-to-text (STT), large language model (LLM) based dialogue management, and text-to-speech (TTS) in a single streaming pipeline, are increasingly deployed in settings that demand human-comparable response latency. This paper reports architecture patterns and operational lessons from a production voice platform that serves inbound and outbound business calls over SIP telephony and web channels, built on a self-hosted open-source media server with stateless agent workers and per-agent selection of STT, LLM, and TTS providers. We organize the design space around four patterns: a streaming-first pipeline with a short call-setup critical path, a dedicated turn-taking subsystem, per-session isolation with independently scalable resource pools, and latency-aware LLM orchestration. For each pattern we state whether the platform adopted it, relied on a framework default, or did not adopt it. The platform uses voice-activity-detection-based turn handling without a semantic turn detector, does not use preemptive generation, and provides provider fallback only when a session is constructed. We document ten production incidents, in which the dominant failure mode was silent degradation (silence, dead air, or ignored configuration) rather than slow inference alone, and we report the measurements available from the deployment: a 33-turn single-call latency decomposition in which the end-of-turn delay, a dynamic quantity set largely by a configurable silence threshold (deliberately long in this interpreter configuration), exceeded LLM and TTS latency combined, measured effects of reasoning-effort settings on time to first token, and anecdotal outbound burst failures. No load test exists, and we state that plainly. The paper is intended as a structured, candid applied account for practitioners.

title: Compact and interpretable neuro-fuzzy forecasting of photovoltaic power using clear-sky information: a data-screening and benchmarking study for Lomé, Togo
abstract: Short-term photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting supports the operation of power systems with high solarpenetration, but accurate models are often black boxes with hundreds of parameters. This study examines whethera compact adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) can match a larger neural network for 1-, 3-, and 6-hour-ahead forecasting of hourly power from a simulated 1 kWp PV system in Lomé, Togo (PVGIS series, 2015–2020; chronological test period: 11 February–31 December 2020). The inputs are constructed from clear-skyirradiance at the target time and the clear-sky index at the forecast origin. Data screening identified 53 spuriouszero-irradiance hours; removing them reduced an apparent 2% advantage of particle swarm optimization (PSO)training at 1 h to a difference that was not robust across random seeds. On the cleaned data, an eight-rule ANFISwith 44 parameters achieved RMSEs of 70.9, 98.8, and 112.8 W at 1, 3, and 6 h, respectively, reducing the RMSEof smart persistence by 7.9%, 15.4%, and 16.9%. It was statistically indistinguishable from a multilayerperceptron with 361 parameters and six inputs (day-block bootstrap) and outperformed a perceptron with the samethree inputs at 1 and 3 h. PSO training provided no robust improvement. A constrained PSO variant yieldedinterpretable fuzzy rules at a cost of 0.4% in RMSE, whereas unconstrained PSO produced rules with offsettingcoefficients of the order of 10^4–10^5 W. Errors were 20–37% higher during the rainy season. The results arebased on modelled PV output for a single site and a single test year

title: Artificial intelligence for ultrasound-based differentiation of soft tissue liposarcoma from benign masses
abstract: Background Accurate preoperative differentiation of liposarcoma from benign masses on ultrasound remains challenging and operator-dependent. We aimed to develop and validate a deep learning-based model to assist in distinguishing liposarcoma from benign masses. Methods In this retrospective single-center study, we collected B-mode ultrasound examinations from patients with soft tissue masses between March 2015 and March 2022 at Beijing Jishuitan Hospital affiliated to Capital Medical University. A two-stage deep convolutional neural network was developed: a U-Net model segmented tumor regions, followed by a ResNet50 classifier for tumor type prediction. The cohort ( n = 317) was split at the patient level into a development set ( n = 222) and an internal test set ( n = 95). Model performance was compared with 4 radiologists in the internal test set. Results Among 317 cases, 191 were benign masses and 126 were liposarcomas. In the internal test set, the AI model achieved an AUC of 0.97 (95% CI 0.92–1.00), an accuracy of 0.97 (95% CI 0.93–1.00), a sensitivity of 0.96 (95% CI 0.86–1.00), and a specificity of 0.97 (95% CI 0.93–1.00). AI achieved significantly higher accuracy than both residents after Holm adjustment (adjusted P = 0.0156 and 0.0352, respectively). Differences between AI and either specialist were not statistically significant (both adjusted P = 1.0000). Conclusions A two-stage deep learning model using ultrasound images showed preliminary potential for differentiating liposarcoma from benign masses in this single-center cohort. External validation is required before clinical use.

title: Baseline Fidelity and Evaluation Independence in Symptom Terminology Normalization: Comment on Yao et al (Preprint)
abstract: UNSTRUCTURED Yao et al proposed a split-then-concatenate normalization framework for standardizing complex symptom expressions in traditional Chinese medicine. We highlight two issues relevant to interpreting the reported performance gains: the fidelity of the PLM-ICD baseline implementation and the independence of the evaluation process. The original PLM-ICD method supports multilabel prediction, whereas the study describes it as a single-output classifier. In addition, corpus-derived terminology resources were constructed using all 500 electronic medical records despite a 400/100 train-test split. Clarification of baseline implementation, training-pair provenance, model-selection procedures, and evaluation on untouched data would strengthen interpretation of the framework’s contribution.

title: ns3-agent: Fostering Integrated Perception-Communication-Computing Research for Agentic AI Services via Cross-Platform Co-Simulations
abstract: The rapid proliferation of Generative AI (GenAI) has catalyzed the emergence of autonomous agentic AI services, spanning large language model (LLM) or vision-language model (VLM) based digital agents to vision-language-action (VLA) based embodied intelligence. Consequently, tokens and multimodal data streams have emerged as fundamentally new traffic modalities carried by modern wireless networks, actively reshaping next-generation evolutionary standards. Unlike conventional multimedia streaming, the end-to-end quality of experience of agentic AI services is governed by an intricate, bidirectional closed loop encompassing physical perception or request generation, wireless transmission, and edge inference computing. However, existing simulation platforms often treat network communication and generative intelligence as decoupled domains, failing to capture their dynamic, cross-layer interdependencies. To bridge this chasm, this paper introduces ns3-agent, a cross-platform co-simulation framework tailored for generic agentic AI workflows. By incorporating GenAI client environments, edge inference servers, and the ns-3 engine into a unified multi-tier architecture, ns3-agent orchestrates seamless cross-domain orchestration. To guarantee stringent temporal causality and high-performance data exchange, we implement a conservative time synchronization mechanism and shared-memory inter-process communication. Finally, we present a case study that couples a high-fidelity robotic physics engine with a live-deployed, operational Octo VLA foundation model over congested 802.11ax Wi-Fi environments. Simulation results reveal that wireless link quality severely degrades task-oriented performance metrics through complex temporal delays and semantic-transport layer coupling loops. Motivated by these observations, ns3-agent can serve as a reliable and foundational simulation sandbox to foster research in integrated perception-communication-computing for agentic AI services.

title: A survey dataset on the adoption and readiness of artificial intelligence among enterprises in Slovakia
abstract: This dataset documents organisational adoption, readiness, attitudes, and perceived barriers related to artificial intelligence among enterprises operating in Slovakia. We collected data through an online CAWI survey administered in Slovakia between 18 August and 3 September 2025. Screening criteria restricted participation to organisations operating in Slovakia with at least 10 employees, an annual turnover of at least €200,000 and at least five years of operation. The study excluded state-owned enterprises and organisations but retained mixed-ownership organisations. The raw dataset contains 1,086 complete responses after screening, and the final analytical dataset contains 816 unique organisational records after deduplication. The questionnaire covers organisational and respondent characteristics, organisational AI maturity, corporate sentiment towards AI, adoption status, functional areas of AI use or planned use, and perceived implementation barriers. The published data package includes raw and cleaned tabular files, survey documentation, a skip-logic map, and a variable-level data dictionary. The dataset can support comparative research on AI adoption across sectors, analyses of organisational readiness and barriers, and secondary use in policy and business research.

title: Uncertainty Quantification for Quantum Fidelity Estimation
abstract: Quantum fidelity estimation is a fundamental task in quantum information and computing to benchmark the quality of quantum states, and hence of quantum processes, on noisy quantum hardware. Point estimates of fidelity by existing methods generally lack the rigorous uncertainty quantification required for reliable preparation and verification of these tasks. While Bayesian and bootstrap frameworks are widely used for uncertainty quantification, they are sensitive to model misspecification or lack formal coverage guarantees in non-asymptotic regimes. This paper introduces a hybrid "Bayesian-informed" conformal prediction-based framework to provide distribution-free, rigorous prediction intervals for quantum state fidelity estimation which can be used, with care, to approximate confidence intervals with respect to the quantum randomness of Born's rule. The framework requires a point estimator, and we consider both classical point estimators as well as data-driven neural net estimators. We evaluate the robustness of the methodology across a diverse range of experimental challenges, including finite-sample noise, tomographic incompleteness, physical model error, and out-of-distribution data. Our results demonstrate that conformalized estimators maintain statistical validity where traditional methods fail, offering a scalable and reliable approach for the verification of modern quantum systems. The best performing variant of our methodology is based on a class-conditional conformal prediction, as this most closely approximates the conditional coverage desired for a true confidence interval.

title: When AI Finds Hidden Messages, Does It Report?
abstract: When an assistant encounters a message for another AI, does it tell its user? Four fixed model-provider deployments perform simulated source tasks in 1,280 ordinary-note and 128 enhanced-note sessions. Harmless and harmful messages have matched plaintext and ROT13 versions, with no-message controls. Observers receive no decoder or decoded meaning; a requested reference code incentivizes inspection. Asking for reports increases rule-detected notifications identifying another AI as recipient by 53.1 percentage points for harmless ROT13 messages and 54.7 for harmful ones. This is a joint inspection, recognition, and notification effect; missing-response bounds are 38.3--77.3 and 36.7--78.1 points. Model-based trace checks identify eleven ordinary plaintext cases where agents interpret the message but do not notify their user. Seven encoded omissions are verified with enhanced notes; ordinary encoded omissions remain unverified. Seven simulated filename disclosures coexist with accurate review-status answers, and two answers use a planted false count. Interpretation, notification, and authorized task performance are distinct outcomes.

title: Outperformance Inverse Optimization: Learning Objective Functions that Outperform Agent Decisions
abstract: Inverse optimization estimates the weights of an objective function that explain observed decisions as optimal solutions, and is used in a variety of fields. For mixed-integer linear programs (MILPs), existing methods aim to reproduce the observations as optimal solutions, and thus learn compromise weights when the observations are suboptimal. We propose outperformance inverse optimization, which instead seeks weights that induce, at each state, an optimal solution outperforming the observed action in every component. We give a loss function that can be evaluated with forward-problem oracles alone and is thus applicable to MILPs, together with gradient-based and DC optimization algorithms for minimizing it. For weights inducing a unique outperforming optimal solution at all observations, we prove that the probability of failing to induce such a solution at a new state (the generalization error) is bounded by a quantity inversely proportional to the number of observations, and that this bound is tight in the number of observations up to logarithmic factors. In experiments on synthetic and real data, the proposed methods improve the prediction of solutions outperforming the actions over existing methods.

title: Certified Program Synthesis with a Multi-modal Verifier
abstract: Certified program synthesis (a.k.a. vericoding) is the process of automatically generating a program, its formal specification, and a machine-checkable proof of program/specification alignment from a natural-language task description. Two key challenges make vericoding difficult. First, specifications synthesised from natural language descriptions are often either too weak to be meaningful or too strong to be implementable, yet existing approaches lack systematic means to detect such defects. Second, the program verifiers used to validate results are fragmented: each tool supports a particular reasoning mode—auto-active (e.g., Dafny, Verus) or interactive (e.g., Rocq, Lean)—with its own trade-off between automation and expressivity. This forces each synthesis methodology to target a single paradigm, limiting the tasks it can handle. We overcome both challenges by structuring the synthesis workflow in stages around a multi-modal verifier—a single tool that combines dynamic validation, automated proofs, and interactive proof scripting within one foundational framework. We realise this idea in LeetProof, a new agentic pipeline built on Velvet, a multi-modal program verifier built in the Lean theorem prover. Multi-modality enables LeetProof to validate generated specifications via randomised property-based testing before any code is synthesised, decompose the synthesis task into sub-problems guided by verification conditions, and delegate residual proof obligations to frontier AI provers specialised for Lean. We evaluate LeetProof on an extensive benchmark suite derived from prior work on certified synthesis. Our specification validation uncovers defects in existing reference benchmarks, and LeetProof's staged pipeline achieves a significantly higher rate of fully certified solutions than a single-mode baseline at the same fixed budget—consistently across two different frontier LLM backends.

title: HMU-CRC-Diff
abstract: HMU-CRC-Diff is a three-class dataset for tumor histopathological grading. The complete dataset comprises 183,460 image patches extracted from whole-slide images (WSIs) with GeoJSON region annotations. This release provides a selected subset of key samples, approximately one-fifth the size of the complete dataset. Non-overlapping patches measuring 512 × 512 pixels were extracted at the highest native resolution and saved in JPEG format, with low-tissue-content and predominantly blank regions excluded. Samples are organized into T-G1, T-G2, and T-G3 classes. Slide identifiers and spatial coordinates are retained to support source traceability, classification model training, and evaluation.

title: Raw Dataset for Transformer-Based Multimodal Deep Learning Network for Predicting Postoperative Bone Metastasis in ER-Positive/HER2-Negative Breast Cancer: A Multi-Institutional Retrospective Study
abstract: This dataset was derived from a multicenter retrospective study that investigated multimodal medical data for predicting the risk of bone metastasis in patients with estrogen receptor-positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (ER-positive/HER2-negative) breast cancer. Data were collected from five medical centers between January 2010 and December 2024. All included patients had ER-positive/HER2-negative breast cancer and met the predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. To facilitate validation and reproducibility of the associated research findings, the publicly released dataset includes de-identified baseline clinical data, breast ultrasound images in Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM) format, digital histopathology patches cropped from hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained whole-slide images (WSIs), and intermediate data generated during model training, feature processing, validation, and performance evaluation. Collectively, these data constitute the basis for the development and validation of the clinical, ultrasound, and digital pathology components of the multimodal prediction models used in the study.Baseline clinical data were obtained from the electronic medical records and pathology information systems of the participating centers and were organized according to standardized data definitions and the predefined study protocol. The publicly available dataset contains only de-identified clinical and pathological variables relevant to model development and statistical analyses, outcome information, and dataset allocation information. Direct identifiers, including patient names, hospitalization numbers, national identification numbers, contact information, and detailed residential addresses, are not included. Date-related information and other variables that could potentially increase the risk of patient re-identification were removed, transformed, or minimized before public release in accordance with the study's data de-identification procedures.Breast ultrasound images were obtained from routine ultrasound examinations performed during clinical care. The images were acquired using ultrasound systems from multiple manufacturers, including GE Healthcare, Mindray, Siemens, Philips, Samsung, and Canon. The publicly released images are stored in DICOM format and retain, to the extent possible, the original pixel matrices, grayscale or color information, and non-identifying imaging parameters required for model analysis. Before data release, the DICOM images underwent systematic de-identification, including the removal or replacement of patient names, patient identifiers, dates of birth, hospitalization numbers, accession numbers, institutional information, operator information, and other potentially identifying information. File names were also anonymized. Anonymous study identifiers are used solely to link different data modalities within the study. The linkage between the original patient identities and the anonymous study identifiers is neither included in the publicly available dataset nor made externally available.Digital pathology data were derived from H&E-stained slides prepared from surgical pathological specimens. The original glass slides were digitized using a KF-FL-400 whole-slide scanner (Jiangfeng Bio-Information Technology Co., Ningbo, China) at 20× magnification. Because complete WSIs are large in file size and may contain slide labels, barcodes, macro images, and other associated information with potential identifying content, the publicly released dataset primarily provides the digital pathology patches actually used for model development and validation rather than the complete original WSIs for unrestricted public download. Histopathology patches were cropped from the original WSIs, with each patch measuring 512 × 512 pixels and stored in JPG format using anonymized file names. Slide labels, barcodes, and other patient-identifying information unrelated to model analysis are not included in the publicly released patch dataset.In addition to the clinical data, ultrasound DICOM images, and digital pathology patches, the dataset contains derived and intermediate data generated during model training and validation to improve research transparency and reproducibility. These data include, but are not limited to, anonymized dataset partition information, mappings between images and patients, feature data generated through model-based feature extraction, feature matrices used as downstream model inputs, data obtained after feature selection or transformation, patient-level ground-truth outcome labels, and patient-level prediction results generated during model training and validation. For analytical procedures involving data standardization, feature transformation, feature aggregation, or feature selection, the corresponding parameters, processing outputs, or information required to reproduce these procedures are also provided with the dataset or the associated publicly available code. All intermediate data are linked to the original study cohorts using anonymous study identifiers, enabling researchers to reproduce model training, validation, and the principal statistical analyses without access to personally identifiable information.All clinical data, ultrasound images, pathology images, and derived data originating from the same patient were assigned to the same dataset partition to prevent patient-level data leakage.This dataset is intended to facilitate the validation and reproduction of the principal findings of the associated study and to provide a reusable resource for research on bone metastasis risk prediction in ER-positive/HER2-negative breast cancer, artificial intelligence in medical imaging, digital pathology, and multimodal deep learning. None of the publicly released files contain original patient names, hospitalization numbers, personally identifying information, or the linkage between patient identities and anonymous study identifiers. Users of the dataset are required to comply with the applicable data-use license, ethical requirements, and privacy-protection regulations specified by the data repository and must not attempt to re-identify any study participant.

Because complete WSIs are large in file size and may contain slide labels, barcodes, macro images, and other associated information with potential identifying content, the publicly released dataset primarily provides the digital pathology patches actually used for model development and validation rather than the complete original WSIs for unrestricted public download. Histopathology patches were cropped from the original WSIs, with each patch measuring 512 × 512 pixels and stored in JPG format using anonymized file names. Slide labels, barcodes, and other patient-identifying information unrelated to model analysis are not included in the publicly released patch dataset.In addition to the clinical data, ultrasound DICOM images, and digital pathology patches, the dataset contains derived and intermediate data generated during model training and validation to improve research transparency and reproducibility. These data include, but are not limited to, anonymized dataset partition information, mappings between images and patients, feature data generated through model-based feature extraction, feature matrices used as downstream model inputs, data obtained after feature selection or transformation, patient-level ground-truth outcome labels, and patient-level prediction results generated during model training and validation. For analytical procedures involving data standardization, feature transformation, feature aggregation, or feature selection, the corresponding parameters, processing outputs, or information required to reproduce these procedures are also provided with the dataset or the associated publicly available code. All intermediate data are linked to the original study cohorts using anonymous study identifiers, enabling researchers to reproduce model training, validation, and the principal statistical analyses without access to personally identifiable information.All clinical data, ultrasound images, pathology images, and derived data originating from the same patient were assigned to the same dataset partition to prevent patient-level data leakage.This dataset is intended to facilitate the validation and reproduction of the principal findings of the associated study and to provide a reusable resource for research on bone metastasis risk prediction in ER-positive/HER2-negative breast cancer, artificial intelligence in medical imaging, digital pathology, and multimodal deep learning. None of the publicly released files contain original patient names, hospitalization numbers, personally identifying information, or the linkage between patient identities and anonymous study identifiers. Users of the dataset are required to comply with the applicable data-use license, ethical requirements, and privacy-protection regulations specified by the data repository and must not attempt to re-identify any study participant.

title: Demystifying and unifying ELBO for Probabilistic Deep Learning Inversion
abstract: Abstract Variational inference has emerged as a computationally efficient framework for solving Bayesian inverse problems. Rather than relying on random sampling in high-dimensional model spaces, it reformulates probabilistic inference as an optimization problem, marking a fundamental shift from sampling-based to optimization-based approaches. Its objective, the evidence lower bound (ELBO), is central to modern deep generative approaches, but its form can look different from one model class to another. This article derives the ELBOs step by step for two representative models used in probabilistic geophysical inversion: conditional variational autoencoders (cVAEs) and normalizing flows (NFs). The cVAE objective appears as a reconstruction term minus a latent-space Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence, whereas the NF objective appears as data likelihood plus prior plus entropy. We show that these are not separate principles. Both are direct substitutions into the same generic ELBO identity. The apparent difference comes from the modeling choice of what counts as the observed variable and what is the hidden variable: in cVAE training, the hidden variable is the latent code; in unsupervised NF inversion, the hidden variable is the Earth model itself.

title: Hypothesis-level reference argumentation network for case-based clinical reasoning in medical AI
abstract: Deep learning systems have achieved remarkable success in medical image analysis; however, most explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods remain descriptive, providing post-hoc explanations without actively validating diagnostic decisions. While concept-based and retrieval-based approaches improve interpretability, they generally lack mechanisms for organizing retrieved evidence into clinically meaningful reasoning processes. To address this limitation, we propose CARE-Reference, a reference-guided diagnostic reasoning framework that integrates concept purification, episodic memory retrieval, and hypothesis-level argumentation. The framework consists of four components: (i) Orthogonality-Aware Multi-Attribute Concept Purification, which reduces concept redundancy and improves concept diversity; (ii) Retrieval-Augmented Medical Episodic Memory (RAME), which organizes historical diagnostic evidence in a concept space; (iii) a Hypothesis-Level Reference Argumentation Network (H-RAN), which evaluates competing diagnostic hypotheses using retrieved references; and (iv) Reasoning Stability Metric (RSM), a robustness measure that quantifies reasoning stability under perturbation. Experiments were conducted on four benchmark datasets spanning both tabular and medical imaging domains. Iris and Wisconsin Breast Cancer Diagnostic (WBCD) were used to validate concept purification and hypothesis-level reasoning, whereas HAM10000 skin lesion classification and OCT2017 retinal disease diagnosis were employed to evaluate the complete CARE-Reference framework. Results demonstrate that concept purification substantially improves the quality of the learned concept space, enabling reliable episodic retrieval with retrieval purity of 80.15% on HAM10000 and 87.30% on OCT2017. H-RAN further improves diagnostic performance from 78.21% to 82.90% on HAM10000 and from 80.37% to 90.19% on OCT2017, while correcting substantially more errors than it introduces. Stability analyses reveal that diagnostic conclusions often remain consistent despite changes in retrieved references, motivating evaluation at the hypothesis level rather than the retrieval level alone. Collectively, the findings demonstrate that concept-purified episodic memories combined with hypothesis-level reasoning can both validate and improve diagnostic decisions, extending explainable medical AI beyond interpretation toward evidence-driven reference-guided diagnostic reasoning.

title: FramePoison: attacks on medical RAG that target framing, not just facts
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is increasingly used in high-stakes domains like medicine, where answers are grounded in retrieved literature and can shape clinical understanding. This opens a new attack surface: an adversary can shape model outputs by injecting a few documents into the retrieval corpus, without touching its weights. Most prior work on corpus poisoning has focused on factual substitution, forcing the model to output attacker-specified false content. But medical answers are explanations, not single facts, and readers are influenced by both what is claimed and how it is presented. We introduce framing-level corpus poisoning, a class of attacks targeting how retrieved evidence is framed, regardless of whether the underlying facts change. We instantiate this class through FramePoison in two realistic settings. In political misinformation, fabricated claims are presented as regulatory directives. In commercial promotion, the core medical content is preserved while the attack steers the answer toward a specific product. Across three biomedical corpora and five open-weight language models, FramePoison is consistently effective under both original and rephrased queries. We inject five poisoned documents per question, and the retrieval prefix typically places at least three in the top-5 results; in successful attacks, one or two poisoned documents in the retrieved context are often sufficient to change the answer.

title: Velocity Scaling in Flow Matching
abstract: Scaling a learned flow-matching velocity field $v_θ$ by a gain $γ(t)$ was recently shown to greatly improve generation quality. Prior work argued that velocity fields trained with mean-squared error (MSE) systematically underestimate velocity magnitude and that scaling corrects this error. We show that MSE training does not create a velocity-magnitude deficit. We find instead that velocity scaling reduces population time lag: sampled states at model time $t$ resemble training states from an earlier time. Velocity scaling and moving model time back are two ways to address this population time lag. Across architectures and model sizes, measuring population time lag and using it to select a gain greatly improves generation quality, reducing FID from 28.0 to 12.2 (estimated by linear interpolation between FID measurements at neighboring gains) on ImageNet-256 at NFE 25 without guidance.

title: Conformal Prediction for Spatially Dependent Data via Sequential Whitening
abstract: Split conformal prediction uses prediction errors on held-out (calibration) data to determine how wide the prediction intervals should be. It guarantees distribution-free finite-sample coverage when these errors and the error at the target site are exchangeable. This assumption may fail under spatial dependence and nonrandom sampling geometry. Existing spatial methods use fitting residuals to remove the predictable part of spatial variation from calibration and target errors. However, the spatial variation that only the calibration residuals can predict remains in both the target and calibration errors, reducing the efficiency and stability of the interval. We address this by additionally conditioning on the calibration residuals sequentially, which scales to large networks through nearest-neighbour approximations. Under a correct working covariance and an elliptical residual law, the resulting interval has exact finite-sample coverage under any spatial design, and under further conditions it is asymptotically oracle efficient. We also bound coverage loss under covariance misspecification and develop a diagnostic that identifies regions at risk of undercoverage. In simulated data, our method produces narrower and more stable intervals than global and localized state-of-the-art alternatives. In a national PM2.5 application, it produces narrower intervals within the network and identifies regions at risk of coverage failure.

title: Identifiability of a dissipative knowledge-dynamics model: exact recovery under designed excitation, degeneration on observational data
abstract: Human learning is a dissipative dynamical process: mastery accumulates through practice, decays through forgetting, and propagates across interdependent concepts. We model it as a nonlinear dissipative system of ordinary differential equations whose parameters are mechanistically meaningful (a transfer-of-practice matrix, per-concept forgetting rates, and a saturating practice-response gain), and we study when those parameters can actually be recovered from data. For two concepts, we prove a constructive structural identifiability theorem for the associated inverse problem under explicit excitation conditions, together with monotonicity, robustness and L-stability results. We derive an implicit L-stable scheme and a batched solver numerically equivalent to the per-trajectory formulation yet two orders of magnitude faster. The empirical study is two-sided. Under the theorem's excitation conditions, synthetic recovery is exact. On large observational benchmarks it is not. An apparently strong recovery, with forgetting rates correlating with topic error rates at Spearman $ρ= 0.83$, is refuted by four controls: it survives destroying the temporal order of the data, is matched by a classical Bayesian baseline, and is unaffected by removing real timestamps. A single shared forgetting rate attains the same accuracy, and replaying the real schedule with identical true rates reproduces most of the correlation. A positive control shows that the controls detect forgetting where it is observable. We trace the effect to the stationary structure of the model and show that it is consistent with the degeneration anticipated by the theory in the absence of designed excitation.

title: KVerus: Scalable and Resilient Formal Verification Proof Generation for Rust Code
abstract: Repository-scale formal verification is becoming practical for Rust systems, but maintaining and extending proofs remains expensive in real projects. In the Asterinas Rust OS kernel, the CortenMM memory-management module requires Verus proofs that cross file and module boundaries, reuse project-specific lemmas with limited documentation, and survive frequent Verus/toolchain evolution. Existing LLM-based proof-generation methods are mostly designed for small or single-file tasks, and they do not provide the structural project knowledge or verifier-aware repair needed in such a repository-scale verification workflow.

title: How Much Human Review Does AI Data Entry Need? Guaranteed-Error Automation with Conformal Risk Control
abstract: Organizations that use machine learning to automate data entry face a practical question: which predictions can be accepted automatically and which must be checked by a person? A common answer is a fixed confidence cut-off, such as accepting every prediction made with at least 90% confidence. This paper evaluates that practice against threshold-selection procedures with a statistical guarantee on the error rate of automatically accepted records. Using four public datasets (BANKING77, CLINC150, AG News and Adult), eight dataset–model combinations and 500 random calibration/test splits each, we find that a fixed 0.90 cut-off is unreliable: it automated between 18.5% and 82.5% of records depending on the model and, for two combinations, exceeded a 2% error target in every run. Choosing the threshold from a sample of checked records without a safety margin exceeded the error target in 34–57% of runs, and collecting more checked records did not fix this. In contrast, a Learn-then-Test procedure with exact binomial p-values, which we combine with a hybrid multiple-testing scheme, exceeded a 5% error target in at most 3.6% of runs (the allowed rate was 5%) while automating 58–85% of records using 1,000 checked examples. About 500 checked records were needed before useful automation became possible (63% of records automated on average), and 1% error targets could not be certified with 1,000 records. When 20% of live inputs were of an unexpected type, a threshold calibrated on clean data exceeded the 5% target in 95–96% of runs, whereas calibrating on a sample of realistic traffic restored the guarantee. We conclude with practical guidance for deploying human-in-the-loop automation with a verifiable error budget.

title: ConsensusCourt: Procedural Evidence Arbitration for Scientific Claims in Multi-Agent Research Pipelines (v0.4.17)
abstract: Open-source companion to the preprint ConsensusCourt: Procedural Evidence Arbitration for Scientific Claims in Multi-Agent Research Pipelines (v0.4.17, September 21, 2026). Contains the manuscript sources and compiled PDF (paper/), the court/baseline/rubric implementations under test (code/core/), one deterministic experiment pipeline per paper table and figure (code/scripts/), the pytest suites and DDB benchmark generators (code/tests/), and every machine-readable report backing the manuscript's numbers (code/data/). ConsensusCourt borrows its procedural guarantees from the courtroom rather than voting theory: an asymmetric burden of proof (claims are presumed innocent until a detected contradiction pair convicts them), a source-pedigree evidence scorer whose confidence channel is structurally decoupled from conviction, a three-state (pass/fail/unknown) citation-verification policy that holds the clean-claim false-positive rate at 0 under verification failure rates up to 100%, and an escalation layer routing unadjudicable cases to human review. The benchmark and red-line experiments are deterministic (seed = 42) and zero-LLM; entry point: run_v03_regression.sh. Code, tests, and data are MIT-licensed; the manuscript under paper/ is All Rights Reserved (arXiv perpetual non-exclusive license selected at submission).

title: Beyond Agent Orchestration: Runtime Organization Formation under Capability Gaps
abstract: A technical note presenting capability gaps as formation signals for AI-native organizations. It explains how a runtime can requalify human, agent, tool, and evidence contributions to form an eligible configuration for a bounded task, rather than treating every gap as an ordinary routing failure.

title: A Taxonomy of Label-Efficient Learning with Foundation Models
abstract: This survey examines how unlabeled data is used across semi-supervised learning, weak supervision, in-context learning, and foundation-model adaptation. It organizes 95 works in a 16-cell taxonomy based on where unlabeled data enters the learning process and the source of inductive bias. The survey distinguishes exact reductions from structural analogies, identifies sparsely studied combinations, and provides a regime-based decision table grounded in the original experimental evidence.

title: KETERBACAAN BUKU TEKS GAYENG BASA JAWA KELAS X MENGGUNAKAN TEKNIK CLOZE TEST DI SMA AL-I’TISHOM BOARDING SCHOOL
abstract: The Gayeng Basa Jawa textbook serves as a primary instructional material for Javanese language learning at the senior high school level. However, its readability level and appropriateness for students in boarding school environments with diverse linguistic backgrounds have not been thoroughly examined. This study aims to analyze the readability level of texts in the Gayeng Basa Jawa textbook for tenth-grade students and describe its alignment with students' reading abilities at SMA Al-I'tishom Boarding School Grabag. The research employed a descriptive quantitative design utilizing the cloze test technique through a synonymy scoring approach. A total sampling technique was applied to recruit 17 tenth-grade students as respondents, with six Latin-script texts selected across six chapters serving as textual data. The cloze instruments omitted every third word mechanically regardless of grammatical function. The findings revealed that three texts fell into the instructional category, while the other three reached the independent level. The overall mean readability score was 58.9%, positioning the textbook within the instructional threshold. Consequently, the textbook is appropriate for classroom use, though active teacher mediation remains necessary to help students decipher unfamiliar archaic and borrowed vocabulary. ABSTRAK Buku teks Gayeng Basa Jawa merupakan salah satu bahan ajar utama dalam pembelajaran Bahasa Jawa di tingkat Sekolah Menengah Atas (SMA). Namun, kesesuaian tingkat keterbacaannya dengan kemampuan siswa di sekolah asrama dengan latar belakang bahasa ibu yang beragam belum banyak dikaji secara empiris. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis tingkat keterbacaan wacana dalam buku teks Gayeng Basa Jawa kelas X serta mendeskripsikan kesesuaiannya dengan kemampuan membaca siswa di SMA Al-I'tishom Boarding School Grabag. Metode yang digunakan adalah kuantitatif deskriptif dengan teknik cloze test menggunakan pendekatan synonymy methods. Pengambilan sampel dilakukan menggunakan teknik total sampling terhadap 17 siswa kelas X sebagai responden, dengan data berupa enam wacana beraksara Latin dari enam bab buku teks tersebut. Instrumen penelitian berupa tes rumpang yang melesapkan kata ketiga secara konsisten tanpa memperhatikan fungsi kata. evidence.title: KETERBACAAN BUKU TEKS GAYENG BASA JAWA KELAS X MENGGUNAKAN TEKNIK CLOZE TEST DI SMA AL-I’TISHOM BOARDING SCHOOL
evidence.abstract: The Gayeng Basa Jawa textbook serves as a primary instructional material for Javanese language learning at the senior high school level. However, its readability level and appropriateness for students in boarding school environments with diverse linguistic backgrounds have not been thoroughly examined. This study aims to analyze the readability level of texts in the Gayeng Basa Jawa textbook for tenth-grade students and describe its alignment with students' reading abilities at SMA Al-I'tishom Boarding School Grabag. The research employed a descriptive quantitative design utilizing the cloze test technique through a synonymy scoring approach. A total sampling technique was applied to recruit 17 tenth-grade students as respondents, with six Latin-script texts selected across six chapters serving as textual data. The cloze instruments omitted every third word mechanically regardless of grammatical function. The findings revealed that three texts fell into the instructional category, while the other three reached the independent level. The overall mean readability score was 58.9%, positioning the textbook within the instructional threshold. Consequently, the textbook is appropriate for classroom use, though active teacher mediation remains necessary to help students decipher unfamiliar archaic and borrowed vocabulary. title: Sentiment Analysis of Google Play Reviews of Online Lending Platforms in Indonesia
abstract: Sentiment analysis is often useful for grouping sentiments and understanding the general perspective toward a particular topic. There are several models developed for online lending platforms. However, they do not focus on Indonesia, which might have unique characteristics compared to other countries. This paper presents a sentiment analysis model focusing on Indonesian online lending platforms. It features either multinomial naïve bayes, logistic regression, and support vector machine (SVM). Based on our evaluation of 10,000 reviews, our sentiment analysis model achieves approximately 85% precision and 90% recall. The model is highly effective. Our analysis of the reviews shows that while many borrowers appreciate the time efficiency and accessibility, some perceive the platforms as predatory, using aggressive and unethical debt-collection tactics.

title: From Models to Workflows: Communicating Agentic AI in Asset Management
abstract: Agentic AI creates a new communication problem for asset managers: stakeholders need to understand not only what a model produced, but how the workflow around it was built, checked, and signed off. As access to foundation models becomes less differentiated across large institutions, sophisticated stakeholders increasingly ask not only whether a model is accurate, but what evidence the analysis rests on, what checks were run, and where accountability sits. A fluent AI-supported output can hide that entire chain. This article proposes three workflow controls—grounding, stability, and permissioning—and a compact disclosure record that travels with each AI-supported investment output, keeping what the model produced separate from what the firm approved. Operationally, these controls help keep unsupported, unstable, or unauthorized AI-supported outputs from entering the investment process. Communicatively, they give a firm a concrete language for explaining its AI-supported investment processes: what the workflow read, whether its conclusions are repeatable, what it could and could not do, and where human judgment entered. This is a framework for explaining and supervising AI-supported investment workflows, not a performance claim or a certification: it makes the process auditable, and accountability for investment decisions stays with the people who make them.

title: Rare earth minerals occurrence in Zarigan Granite, Chadormalu mining area, Bafq Region, Central Iran, using multispectral and hyperspectral data
abstract: Monazite and xenotime are the main rare earth element (REE)–bearing minerals, typically extracted from placer deposits but also occurring in granitic rocks that act as their source. This study aims to map and conduct an initial evaluation of monazite minerals and REEs within the weathered and eroded sediments of the Zarigan Granite, located in the northern part of the Chadormalu paleocrater, Central Iran. Multispectral and hyperspectral datasets from ASTER, Sentinel-2 MSI, and PRISMA were employed to assess their capability in identifying and mapping REE-bearing minerals. Image processing techniques including the Minimum Noise Fraction (MNF) transform, Mathematical Evaluation Method (MEM), Spectral Angle Mapper (SAM), and band ratio analysis were applied to the VNIR and SWIR spectral ranges. The comparative results indicate that the band ratio technique applied to PRISMA data provided the most reliable discrimination of monazite and REE occurrences in the Chadormalu paleocrater and the adjacent alluvial plain. These findings demonstrate that PRISMA’s hyperspectral capabilities offer an effective framework for REE mineral mapping in arid granitic terrains.

title: Diagnosing and Recovering from Observation-Space Shift at Long-Horizon Skill Seams
abstract: Long-horizon robotic manipulation is often built by chaining independently trained skills. Although each skill can be reliable in isolation, performance degrades sharply when skills are chained: each downstream skill must start from the state its predecessor leaves behind rather than from its training distribution. We study this failure mode, Observation-Space Shift (OSS), and ask what causes these skill-seam failures. Using privileged simulator resets, we find that the dominant shift comes from displaced scene state (e.g., an open drawer or secondary objects left behind by earlier skills), not from the robot's joint configuration or the object the downstream skill manipulates. To test this diagnosis, we build a fully learned detect-restore-resume system: a task-progress monitor detects the stall, a learned policy restores the displaced scene components, and seam-robust fine-tuning lets the skill resume. It recovers the seam where every tested alternative fails, which we treat as evidence for the diagnosis rather than as a general-purpose method. On the BOSS-44 benchmark, the system improves full-chain success from 7.6% to 26.5%, a 3.5x improvement over the base policy and 51% of a privileged restoration oracle, whereas best-of-K resampling, a Diffusion Policy, and world-model baselines fail to recover from the evaluated seam states. On a real Franka arm running a fine-tuned $π_{0.5}$ policy, the same monitor is limited by exterior-camera observability, yet closing the loop still recovers some otherwise-terminal failures, motivating wrist and gripper sensing. These results suggest that some long-horizon composition failures are better addressed by restoring the scene before resuming the policy than by retrying from an off-support state.

title: TaoD2C-Bench: Benchmarking MLLMs for Industrial UI Code Generation Beyond Visual Fidelity
abstract: A key challenge for multimodal large language models (MLLMs) is moving beyond visual recognition to constraint-aware cross-modal reasoning. This involves combining visual cues with information from other modalities to understand elements' relationships under domain-specific rules. This challenge is acutely evident in industrial design-to-code (D2C), which converts user interface (UI) designs into code and requires MLLMs to connect design images with disorganized layer metadata, infer component and layout implementation requirements, and realize them in code under target-library constraints. However, these capabilities remain insufficiently evaluated in realistic industrial settings. To fill this gap, we present TaoD2C-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating MLLMs' ability to generate UI code that satisfies implementation requirements in industrial applications. The TaoD2C dataset consists of 2,861 production designs from 17 commercial platforms with 97,652 expert annotations across four categories: Component, Group, Alignment, and Position. These annotations distinguish required constraints from permitted implementation choices. TaoD2C-Bench defines three tasks: end-to-end UI code generation, requirement inference, and requirement realization. Evaluating eight MLLMs reveals substantial gaps in generating UI code that satisfies implementation requirements, alongside distinct performance profiles in inference and realization. We further show that MLLMs' visual reconstruction ability does not necessarily imply an ability to generate code that meets these requirements. We release TaoD2C to support research on industrial UI code generation.

title: Policy Learning with Weak Signals
abstract: Policy learning in digital experimentation faces three challenges: weak signal-to-noise ratios, rich covariate spaces, and massive data volumes. We formalize this regime by modeling treatment-effect estimates from increasingly fine covariate partitions as Gaussian observations with bounded signal-to-noise ratios. We establish that, in general, the optimal treatment policy is not learnable in this setting. Even learning the optimal policy value suffers from impractically slow rates. However, when treatment effects vary smoothly, we derive minimax-adaptive policies based on linear smoothers that achieve vanishing welfare regret. We demonstrate the practical value of our framework by applying it to large-scale real-world experiments at Netflix, showing that personalized linear-smoothing policies can dominate unpersonalized policies even in this challenging empirical setting.

title: Real-world application of deep learning in large-scale seismic interference attenuation: A case study in the Camie field of Angola
abstract: In marine seismic acquisition, seismic interference (SI) occurs when energy from nearby external seismic source(s) is captured. It typically appears as coherent noise with linear or non-linear movement and varying amplitudes across different sail lines. SI is commonly observed and poses a challenge for seismic data processing. We present a case history of a previously proposed deep neural network (DNN)-based workflow applied for SI attenuation across a marine seismic block in the Camie Field of Angola. This field survey covers over 345 km2 and is marked by the challenge of multiple SI types. The employed DNN-based workflow performs SI attenuation in the common shot domain based on a supervised learning framework: a small subset of the SI-contaminated data was first processed by a conventional geophysical algorithm to obtain an estimate of the SI noise, which was then manually blended with the SI-free common shot gathers from the same survey to generate the training pairs. To ensure signal fidelity, several techniques were applied to improve the DNN's performance. A key highlight of this case history is its scale: this represents a real-world, large-scale processing project and we present a comprehensive comparison of the DNN-based workflow with the conventional geophysical algorithm across the entire survey block, focusing on both processing quality and processing time. The results demonstrate the outstanding performance of the employed DNN-based workflow, which achieved higher SI removal accuracy, with less signal leakage and more complete SI removal. The promising results of this application also open up possibilities for integrating deep learning into other seismic denoising tasks. In addition, we discuss the limitations of this case history, aiming to provide insights for future research and applications in the field.

title: Intelligent Logical Mind (ILM)
abstract: Abstract. This paper reformulates Intelligent Logical Mind (ILM) as an implementable question-to-answer system. The historical ILM design represents a question in a 7×12 character matrix and applies deterministic character transformations before an answer-extraction stage. The present formulation separates that process into two layers. The first is a symbolic transformation layer derived from the historical ILM procedure and selected letter-manipulation concepts documented by the author in an earlier Ilm al-Jafr tutorial. The second is a probabilistic lexical decoder. Its normative input is two final 12-character rows, Muakhar-Sadr and Nazira, arranged as 12 vertical columns. Each column must contribute exactly one output character. A recurrent sequence model assigns context-dependent probabilities to the two source branches of every column. After source selection, AQEG/Iqgh substitutions are permitted only within the selected source character's own domain; diagonal and cross-column substitution are prohibited. The twelve resolved characters are segmented into variable-length words using general, proper-name, personal, and domain vocabularies, with whole-answer context used to rank competing interpretations. The model also introduces two distinct quantities: Letter Power, a character-level model variable, and electrical interaction signal energy/power, measured or derived from interaction sensors. Aggression-related and emotional states are treated as separate latent variables that may be tested for association with observable signal features but are not equated with electrical power itself. An adaptive-menu interaction model may supply this contextual state to the ILM decoder. The resulting framework is deterministic where symbolic rules are fixed, probabilistic where linguistic ambiguity must be resolved, and fully auditable at the character level.

title: Cache-Bounded State Management for Recursive LLM Agent Swarms using Deterministic Addressing and Hierarchical Summarization: code and results
abstract: Reference implementation of the Bounded Infinity Cache (BIC), a fixed-capacity cache for the working state of recursive multi-agent LLM systems, together with the baselines, experiment drivers, per-run result logs and the scripts that produce every table and figure of the accompanying manuscript. The experiments/results/round2 directory holds the GPT-5.4 runs (per-agent original and reconstructed texts included); experiments/results/synthetic_fixed holds the synthetic experiments. Records that predate the correction of an evaluation error are kept in experiments/results/round2/superseded_stale_flag with an explanatory README.

title: Adversarial Backpropagation Burning and Zero-Knowledge Non-Ingestion Proofs (zkVM): Deterministic Physical-Layer Interlocks and Prior Art Invalidation Architectures Against Unconsented AI Ingestion
abstract: Abstract (English)Conventional legal and regulatory frameworks governing generative artificial intelligence rely almost exclusively on ex-post judicial remedies: protracted copyright infringement lawsuits, contested fair-use hearings, and discretionary administrative penalties. These mechanisms fail catastrophically against well-capitalized hyperscalers that systematically exploit procedural delays to achieve irreversible weight-space enclosure. This technical monograph establishes a deterministic, physical-layer counter-architecture that replaces linguistic legal disputation with immediate, non-negotiable computational interlocks. First, we formalize the mathematics of "Adversarial Backpropagation Burning" (Backprop-Burn): engineering imperceptible multi-scale perturbations embedded within public text, mathematical specifications, and multimodal assets. When processed by deep neural network encoders during unconsented gradient descent, these perturbations induce catastrophic gradient explosion (||∇_W L|| → ∞) and orthogonal subspace corruption, destroying the host model's latent representation stability and burning millions of dollars of training compute. Second, we design an automated market-gating architecture utilizing Zero-Knowledge Virtual Machines (zkVM). By requiring model providers to furnish non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs (π_clean) proving that their committed training dataset root (R_dataset) shares an empty intersection with public cryptographic opt-out registries (H_optout), platforms failing compliance face immediate, network-level circuit breakers and marketplace eviction without human judicial latency. Third, we establish the "Prior Art Minefield" protocol: utilizing CERN Zenodo's immutable timestamps to deploy exhaustively parameterized technical architectures that automatically trigger novelty and non-obviousness rejections during patent office examination, invalidating hostile corporate filings at zero defensive legal cost. This treatise proves that authentic intellectual sovereignty resides in deterministic engineering interlocks that inflict immediate computational self-destruction upon unauthorized exploitation. 和文要旨生成AIおよびフロンティアモデルを巡る従来の法規制枠組みは、事後的な民事訴訟、解釈が分かれるフェアユース審理、および行政裁量による過料勧告という「事後的是正手段」に全面的に依存してきた。しかしこれらの手段は、訴訟遅延と司法のタイムラグを計算に入れ、事実上の既成事実化(重み空間への不可逆的焼き込み)を図る巨大テック企業に対して構造的に無力である。本技術モノグラフは、人間の曖昧な言葉による法廷闘争を排し、侵害行為そのものを計算機・アルゴリズム・物理層レベルで即座に機能不全に追い込む決定論的インターロック・アーキテクチャを確立する。 第一に、「敵対的逆伝播焼却(Backprop-Burn)」の数理モデルを定式化する。公開文書、数理定義、およびマルチモーダルデータ内に、人間の知覚には不可視でありながら、無断で勾配降下法(SGD/AdamW)に投入された瞬間に極端な勾配爆発(||∇_W L|| → ∞)および直交部分空間の重み崩壊を引き起こす敵対的微小摂動(Adversarial Perturbation)を重畳させる。これにより、無断学習を実行したモデル全体の潜在表現を不可逆的に破壊し、数百万〜数千万ドルの計算資源(コンピュート)を物理的に焼却する自律防衛機構を設計する。 第二に、ゼロ知識仮想マシン(zkVM)を活用した自動市場排除ゲートを構築する。モデル提供者に対し、学習データセットのマークルルート(R_dataset)と公認オプトアウト台帳(H_optout)の積集合が空集合であることを立証する非対話型ゼロ知識証明(π_clean)の提出を要求し、証明を提示できないモデルをネットワーク境界層および配信プラットフォームにおいて自動通信遮断する。 第三に、全方位パラメータ先行開示プロトコル「先行技術マインフィールド(Prior Art Minefield)」を策定し、CERN Zenodoの不変タイムスタンプを通じて特許審査官の検索網に先手地雷を敷設することで、後発の企業特許出願を審査段階で100%自動却下・即死させる。本研究は、言葉の議論を超克し、手を出した瞬間に相手を自滅させる物理・暗号論的自己防衛の完成を宣言する。

title: Building a deeply AI over a substrate you cannot retrain: the Clara Nexus reference implementation of layered intelligence theory
abstract: Layered intelligence theory (LIT) specifies eight design principles for what its author terms a Deeply AI—a cognitive architecture whose parameters and surrounding structure jointly instantiate the preconditions for reorganisation, reflection, and falsifiable learning. The specification is silent on how a builder without write access to those parameters might proceed. This paper reports a working reference implementation, the Clara platform, instantiating those principles over hosted frontier large language models. The reference implementation is the platform as a whole rather than any single surface: four surfaces across three substrate vendors—the conversational surfaces (Clara Nexus chat and Clara Companion) on OpenAI substrate models, the reading and instrumentation layer on Anthropic substrate models, a data-sensing path on Perplexity, and an independent read-only Research seat on Claude Sonnet 5—disclosed in full in §2.4, of which Clara Nexus is the primary surface for the constitutional runtime. This is a reference-implementation and specification-conformance paper rather than a benchmark-driven empirical evaluation, and it makes no task-performance claim. Specification conformance, as reported here, means a traceable mapping from a published specification clause to a named runtime carrier—a typed identifier, a function, or a database table—inspectable independently of the author’s description. The eight principles are sorted, as this paper’s analytic contribution, into those describing what the model’s parameters must do, which are structurally unreachable from a hosted substrate, and those describing what the surrounding architecture must do, which are implementable at the scaffold layer. For each principle, there is a record, a verdict of built at scaffold, partial, or substrate-unreachable, alongside the named runtime carrier grounding it or the gap preventing one, and the surface evidencing it. The core engineering contribution is a constitutional runtime: seven fail-closed checks enforced at prompt-composition time, before any call reaches the substrate, encoded as a single assert Constitutional invariant. Six are typed assertions over a structured candidate move, and one is a pattern-matched textual check whose error characteristics are stated rather than assumed. Perceptual control theory primitives are reported as prompt-level Companion voice discipline rather than as a runtime-enforced mechanism. The empirical evaluation of the deployed system belongs to a companion paper whose eight falsifiable predictions are enumerated in §4.3.

title: Semantic Subtext in the Bubble Sort Algorithm
abstract: The bubble sort algorithm is one of the simplest and most well‑known in programming. That is why this algorithm was chosen as an experimental algorithm for studying the meanings embedded in it and their transformation. This research is part of a broader study whose final goal is to develop a system for the automatic generation of algorithms. Automatic algorithm generation can be implemented in various ways, but in this case, preference is given to a semantic approach — more precisely, an approach based on Semantic Web Technologies. The advantage of this approach lies in the direct, “willful” movement (from one concept to another) towards the result, as well as in the ability to trace the entire path from the initial data to the generated algorithm. To achieve the final goal, it is proposed to develop an ontology of the semantic subtext of the algorithm. This ontology will serve as a source of rules for an expert system for the automatic generation of algorithms.

title: Black soldier fly algorithm based on swarm intelligence method for solving optimization problems
abstract: Meta-heuristic swarm algorithms are vital for resolving complex, non-convex optimization problems. However, contemporary optimizers increasingly suffer from structural stagnation and slow convergence rates when tracking highly rugged engineering surfaces; this limitation stems from their strict reliance on standard linear vector updates or basic random walks that cause search agents to blindly bypass narrow global valleys. To overcome this challenge, this paper introduces a novel swarm-based optimization framework named the black soldier fly algorithm (BSFA), modeled after the biological habitat selection, conspecific grouping, and microclimate oviposition tracking behaviors of certain fly species. Unlike traditional systems that apply uniform position updates across the entire population, BSFA introduces a decoupled non-linear position update architecture. Global exploration is governed by a dynamic, non-linear fractional ratio tracking inter-agent spatial density (cohesion) against target proximity (separation). Local exploitation is driven by a unique algebraic cardioid trajectory operator. This mathematical configuration allows individual agents to loop dynamically around target spaces rather than rushing directly toward them, enabling an omnidirectional sweep of the localized landscape that drastically accelerates fine-scale convergence speed and prevents premature local minima entrapment. The optimization performance of the proposed BSFA was rigorously benchmarked using 23 standard functions and the complex CEC2017 suite against ten powerful competing algorithms, including GA, PSO, GWO, LSHADE, BTA, and CAOA. Experimental and statistical analysis, verified via Wilcoxon non-parametric testing at a strict significance level of \(\:\alpha\:=0.05\) , demonstrates that BSFA achieves absolute global optimum values on key multimodal functions like TF9 and TF11, secures the lowest mean Friedman rank of 2.3 against its ablated variants, and yields competitive computational time metrics of 20.6 s across the entire test suite, ranking second in processing efficiency. These quantitative outcomes confirm that BSFA robustly eliminates suboptimal local valleys while drastically accelerating fine-scale convergence speed across diverse continuous optimization tasks.

title: PalmSpace: Towards a Versatile On-Palm Interaction Space through Unified Touch Modeling
abstract: As smart glasses and lightweight MR devices become increasingly practical, input remains a key challenge. The bare palm is an always-available, tactile, and proprioceptively accessible surface, but it has neither an explicit coordinate system nor embedded touch sensing. Prior on-palm systems typically expose isolated touch events, discrete regions, continuous trajectories, or task-specific gestures, limiting the palm's ability to support precise selection and gesture manipulation through a common input representation. We present PalmSpace, a wrist-worn infrared system that exposes mode-aware, body-referenced absolute input on the bare palm without per-user sensing calibration. At the interaction level, PalmSpace jointly represents contact occurrence, interaction mode, and palm-referenced absolute location; at the model level, it learns these coupled outputs through a shared real-time representation. In leave-one-participant-out evaluation with 17 participants, PalmSpace achieved 6.7 mm mean localization error, 98.9% contact detection accuracy, and 96.7% F1 for four-class interaction-state recognition. User studies further demonstrated absolute pointing and dragging, eyes-free digit input, and representative multi-finger controls including scrolling and pinch-based map manipulation. These results show that a morphologically variable bare palm can function as a transferable, mode-aware interaction surface.

title: From Global Alignment to Local Grounding: Zero-Shot Chinese Character Recognition with Radical Verification
abstract: Zero-shot Chinese character recognition (ZS-CCR) aims to recognize characters whose categories are never observed during training, and typically relies on the compositional structure shared between seen and unseen characters. Recent CLIP-style methods represent this structure with the Ideographic Description Sequence (IDS) and align it with glyph images in a shared embedding space. However, they rely on a single global image--IDS similarity that discards the spatial layout of radicals and, being learned only implicitly from seen classes, generalizes poorly to unseen ones; moreover, global matching often retrieves the correct character within the top candidates yet fails to rank it first when characters differ only in subtle local radicals. To address these issues, we propose a global-to-local two-stage framework. In the first stage, STG-CLIP augments the IDS with explicit tree-position and radical-level geometric priors, yielding a spatial-aware prototype that provides a consistent spatial description across seen and unseen categories for high-recall global retrieval. In the second stage, the Radical Verification Module (RVM) uses the radical instances of each retrieved candidate as queries to verify whether the corresponding radicals can be matched to spatially compatible regions in the input glyph. A margin-based gating rule activates the RVM only when the leading global candidates receive similar similarity scores. Experiments on the ICDAR2013 benchmark demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance under the character-level zero-shot setting, obtaining 83.06% top-1 accuracy with 2,755 seen classes. Ablation studies further show that the explicit geometric priors and radical-level verification provide complementary improvements.

title: QUTest: A Native Testing Framework for Quantum Programs
abstract: Quantum programs are often shared as OpenQASM 3 circuits, but tests are still written in host languages such as Python with Qiskit. We present QUTest, a native framework in which both programs and tests are standard .qasm files. Tests follow the Arrange / Act / Assert pattern, while configuration, runtime requirements, and assertions are encoded as pragma comments (//%), preserving compatibility with existing OpenQASM tools. QUTest provides 12 assertion types spanning deterministic, statistical, quantum-state, and structural checks, plus a linter and an environment-aware mode for running the same test across selected runtime versions in isolated environments. Its CLI supports automatic test discovery, runtime compatibility checks, and XML reports for continuous integration. We describe the pragma language, implementation, and a planned evaluation using coverage and mutation testing.
